questions.q: What do HTML and CSS describe?
options: Step-by-step instructions that run top to bottom
HTML describes what content is; CSS describes how matching things should look, and the browser works out layout and paints
questions.explain: They're descriptions, not programs; the browser decides the rest.

questions.q: Why can the same page work on a phone, a 4K screen and a screen reader?
options: You give the browser information and it decides layout for the device
questions.explain: You're not controlling the browser, you're giving it information.

questions.q: Which pair of files makes a working first page with no build step?
questions.explain: Double-click index.html to open it; no server or dependencies needed.

questions.q: Why learn to serve a folder over HTTP (e.g. python3 -m http.server)?
options: Some later features such as fetching JSON and certain loading rules behave differently on file:// URLs
questions.explain: Everything in Level 1 works on file://.

questions.q: What does <!doctype html> do?
options: Signals standards mode; without it browsers switch to quirks mode
questions.explain: It's case-insensitive, and not a tag.

questions.q: Why set <html lang="en">?
options: Screen readers pick a pronunciation voice, hyphens: auto and translation tools rely on it
questions.explain: Use BCP 47 tags such as en, en-GB, pt-BR; you can override on any element.

questions.q: Where must <meta charset="utf-8"> appear?
options: Within the first 1024 bytes, so put it first in <head>
questions.explain: The browser only looks that far before guessing.

questions.q: What does <head> hold versus <body>?
options: <head> holds metadata about the document, mostly invisible; <body> holds the content
questions.explain: The parser would insert them anyway, but write them.

questions.q: Why does semantic HTML matter?
options: Assistive technology can navigate it, search engines understand it and your CSS gets simpler
It removes the need for CSS
questions.explain: The accessibility tree for div soup is one undifferentiated run of text.

questions.q: Which heading rules hold up in practice?
options: One h1 per page, don't skip levels going down, choose the level by structure not size
questions.explain: If an h2 should look small, style it small.

questions.q: Why is <span onclick> 'Read more' a problem?
options: It isn't a link, so it can't be reached with the Tab key
questions.explain: Use <a href> for navigation.

questions.q: How does HTML treat runs of whitespace?
options: Collapses any run of spaces, tabs and newlines into one space
questions.explain: Blank lines in source don't create paragraphs.

questions.q: What is the difference between alt="" and a missing alt?
options: Empty tells assistive tech to skip the image; missing makes many screen readers read the file name
questions.explain: Use alt="" for purely decorative images.

questions.q: Why write width and height on every img?
options: The browser reserves space, preventing layout shift when the image arrives (CLS)
questions.explain: Combine with img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }.

questions.q: What should alt text for a chart say?
options: The takeaway, e.g. 'Sales doubled between March and June', with the data in text or a table nearby
questions.explain: Describe what the image communicates in context.

questions.q: What should you avoid starting alt text with?
options: 'Image of…' or 'Picture of…', since the role is already announced
questions.explain: Screen readers already say 'image'.

questions.q: When is a <table> the right element?
options: When the content would make sense in a spreadsheet with meaningful row and column headers
To put things side by side
questions.explain: CSS Grid and Flexbox do layout.

questions.q: What does scope="row" / scope="col" on a th do?
options: Says which cells the header applies to, so a screen reader can announce 'Monday, Close, 17:00'
questions.explain: Without th cells it would announce just '17:00'.

questions.q: Where must <caption> be and what does it become?
options: The first child of the table; its accessible name
questions.explain: It's the table's title.

questions.q: What do colspan and rowspan do?
options: Merge cells across columns or rows
questions.explain: They produce spanning cells like a class schedule.

questions.q: Which fields get submitted with a form?
options: Only those with a name attribute
questions.explain: A field without a name is not submitted.

questions.q: When should you use method="get" versus "post"?
options: get for bookmarkable searches/filters (data in the URL); post for anything that changes data or includes secrets
questions.explain: post sends data in the request body.

questions.q: What are the three jobs of a label?
options: The control's accessible name, a larger click/tap target and visible instructions
questions.explain: Associate with for= matching the input's id, or wrap the input.

questions.q: Why are most broken forms broken?
options: Someone replaced the built-ins with custom controls and didn't rebuild keyboard, autofill, validation and submission
questions.explain: Native form elements handle all of that without JavaScript.

questions.q: What happens with an invalid declaration versus an invalid selector?
options: An invalid selector is ignored alone
An invalid declaration is ignored on its own; an invalid selector makes the whole rule ignored
questions.explain: Forgiving selectors are an exception.

questions.q: What does p.note match?
options: elements with class note (no space means the same element)
questions.explain: A space would make it a descendant selector.

questions.q: Why do most teams avoid IDs for styling?
options: IDs have very high specificity and are unique per page
questions.explain: Classes are the main tool.

questions.q: What does .card.featured match?
questions.explain: class holds a space-separated list.

questions.q: In what order does the cascade compare criteria?
options: Origin/importance, context, style attribute, layers, specificity, then order of appearance
questions.explain: Day to day it's almost always specificity or order.

questions.q: What does !important do to precedence?
options: It reverses origin order for important declarations and jumps above every normal author declaration regardless of specificity
questions.explain: In the test, the weakest selector with !important won.

questions.q: Why does the origin reversal for !important exist?
options: So a user needing high contrast can always override the site
questions.explain: User !important beats author normal.

questions.q: How many values does an element end up with per property?
questions.explain: The cascade picks the winner.

questions.q: What are the four areas of the CSS box, from inside out?
questions.explain: Padding takes the background; margin is always transparent.

questions.q: What does width mean with the default box-sizing: content-box?
options: The content width only; padding and border are added on top
questions.explain: border-box makes width include padding and border.

questions.q: What does padding: 1rem 2rem 0.5rem 0 set?
questions.explain: Two values mean top/bottom and left/right.

questions.q: What are logical properties like margin-inline and padding-block?
options: They follow the text direction: inline is the direction text runs, block is the direction paragraphs stack
questions.explain: In English they're left/right and top/bottom.

questions.q: Which landmarks does the recipe page need?
options: A site header with a labelled nav, one main, a footer and a skip link as the first focusable element
questions.explain: They allow quick navigation by assistive tech.

questions.q: Which list element fits each job?
options: ul for ingredients, ol for steps, dl for facts like servings and timings
questions.explain: Choose the list by meaning.

questions.q: How should the stylesheet be written?
options: One external stylesheet, no style attributes, rem units, border-box sizing and visible :focus-visible styles
questions.explain: The page must also pass html-validate and axe-core.

questions.q: How should the data table behave on small screens?
options: It lives in a region that scrolls horizontally
questions.explain: It also needs a caption and th with scope.

questions.q: Why end a font stack with a generic family?
options: So something sensible appears if no named font matches
questions.explain: Examples: serif, sans-serif, monospace, system-ui.

questions.q: How does font fallback work?
options: Per character: glyphs missing from your web font come from the next font in the stack that has them
questions.explain: Important for multilingual sites.

questions.q: What happens if you ask for italic but declare no italic face?
options: Browsers synthesise a slanted version, which looks worse than a real italic
questions.explain: Declare each face with @font-face.

questions.q: Which format should you serve for web fonts, and what do variable fonts offer?
options: WOFF2; a continuous range of weights (and axes) in one file, e.g. font-weight: 650
questions.explain: Declare the range in @font-face.

questions.q: Why is OKLCH better than HSL for palettes?
options: Its lightness matches perceived brightness, so shades look evenly spaced and contrast is predictable
questions.explain: HSL yellow and blue at the same L look very different in brightness.

questions.q: What does color-mix(in oklch, var(--brand), black 15%) do?
options: Blends the brand colour with 15% black in OKLCH, handy for a hover shade
questions.explain: Relative colour syntax can also take a colour apart into channels.

questions.q: What does rgb(179 64 26 / 50%) mean?
options: The colour at 50% alpha, in modern space-separated syntax
questions.explain: The comma and rgba() forms still work.

questions.q: What responsibility comes with colour, per the lesson?
options: Contrast, which is easy to measure and often ignored
questions.explain: WCAG contrast ratios can be computed.

questions.q: With flex-direction: column, what does justify-content: center do?
options: Centres items vertically, because it works along the main axis
questions.explain: Alignment properties follow the axes, not horizontal and vertical.

questions.q: Three 100px items in a 600px flex container with justify-content: space-between have left offsets of:
questions.explain: First and last touch the edges, with equal gaps between.

questions.q: Which elements become flex items when a container has display: flex?
questions.explain: Grandchildren decide their own layout.

questions.q: When does justify-content have no visible effect?
options: When items have flex-grow and absorb all the free space
questions.explain: It distributes leftover space only.

questions.q: What does flex: 1 expand to?
questions.explain: The basis of 0 is why items end up equal.

questions.q: A 600px container holds items with flex: 1 1 100px and flex: 2 1 200px. Their widths are:
questions.explain: Free space is 300, split 1:2 and added to the bases: 100+100 and 200+200.

questions.q: What is the default flex value (flex: initial)?
options: 0 1 auto: content-sized, can shrink, won't grow
questions.explain: flex: none (0 0 auto) is rigid.

questions.q: How do three items with differing text behave under flex: 1 versus flex: auto in 600px?
options: flex: 1 gives equal widths of 200 each; flex: auto gives unequal widths based on content
questions.explain: flex: auto starts from content size and shares only the extra space.

questions.q: In a 1000px grid with columns 200px 1fr 2fr and a 20px gap, how wide is the 2fr column?
What is the 1fr minimum trap?
options: 1fr means minmax(auto, 1fr), so a track won't shrink below its content's minimum size
fr can't be used with gap
questions.explain: Use minmax(0, 1fr) for truly equal columns.

questions.q: What does fr measure?
options: A fraction of the font size
A fraction of the leftover space after fixed tracks and gaps
questions.explain: Like flex-grow, it shares free space.

questions.q: When should you use Grid rather than Flexbox?
options: For two-dimensional layouts where rows and columns line up
questions.explain: Flexbox arranges items along one line.

questions.q: With only two items in a wide container, how do auto-fit and auto-fill differ?
options: auto-fit collapses empty tracks so the items stretch; auto-fill keeps empty tracks so items stay column-width
questions.explain: At 700px, auto-fit gave 342px items while auto-fill gave about 222px.

questions.q: What does repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr)) do?
options: Makes as many columns as fit, each at least 200px, stretched equally, with no media queries
questions.explain: The count changes with container width.

questions.q: Why write minmax(min(200px, 100%), 1fr)?
options: It stops overflow when the container is narrower than 200px
questions.explain: min() caps the minimum at the container width.

questions.q: When should you prefer auto-fill?
options: When items should keep a consistent size even if the last row is half empty
When items should fill the row
questions.explain: Choose auto-fit when few items should look deliberate.

questions.q: Relative to what is an absolutely positioned element's top/right offset measured?
options: Its containing block: the padding box of the nearest positioned ancestor, else the initial containing block
questions.explain: In the lesson's test the badge landed at the page corner (1260, 0) with no positioned ancestor, and at the card corner (450, 260) once the card had position: relative.

questions.q: What is the main job of position: relative on its own?
options: To fix it to the viewport
To remove the element from flow
To act as an anchor for absolute descendants and let z-index apply, since its space is kept
questions.explain: It moves the element visually without affecting its neighbours.

questions.q: What does position: sticky do?
options: Stays in flow and sticks within its scroll container once a threshold is crossed, until its parent scrolls away
questions.explain: Unlike fixed, it remains in normal flow.

questions.q: What does inset: 0 mean?
questions.explain: It's the shorthand for all four offsets.

questions.q: What does mobile-first mean?
options: Base styles target the narrowest screen, then (width >= …) queries add complexity as space allows
questions.explain: The lesson's grid goes from one to two to three columns at 40rem and 64rem.

questions.q: Why does range syntax (width < 48rem and width >= 48rem) avoid an overlap?
options: max-width: 48rem includes 48rem itself, so pairing it with min-width: 48rem overlaps at exactly 48rem
questions.explain: Range syntax makes the boundary explicit.

questions.q: When are media queries best used?
options: For genuine layout changes, such as collapsing navigation or moving a sidebar, after letting the layout flow with min(), clamp() and auto-fit
questions.explain: Fluid techniques adapt continuously without breakpoints.

questions.q: What does width: min(100% - 2rem, 70rem) with margin-inline: auto give?
options: Gutters plus a maximum width, centred
questions.explain: One line replaces a breakpoint.

questions.q: With :root { --space: 1rem } and .card { --space: 2rem }, what padding does .x { padding: var(--space) } get inside a .card?
options: 32px, because custom properties inherit and are overridden per subtree
questions.explain: The lesson measured 16px at top level and 32px inside .card.

questions.q: What does var(--missing, rgb(0, 0, 255)) compute to?
questions.explain: The fallback is used when the property is undefined.

questions.q: Are custom property names case-sensitive?
questions.explain: Names also start with two dashes.

questions.q: Why are custom properties more than preprocessor variables?
options: They live in the browser, cascade, inherit, change per component or media query, and JavaScript can read and write them
questions.explain: That makes them the base of theming.

questions.q: How is the specifications list built?
options: A dl in an auto-fit grid with no media queries
questions.explain: Requirement 3 of the project.

questions.q: What does subgrid do for the related-product cards?
options: Lines up titles, descriptions and prices across each row
questions.explain: Used inside an auto-fill grid.

questions.q: How should size options be built?
options: Real radio buttons in a fieldset, visually styled as buttons
questions.explain: This keeps native keyboard and screen-reader behaviour.

questions.q: How is the dark theme achieved?
options: One set of semantic custom properties plus color-scheme so form controls follow
questions.explain: Motion is also limited to users who haven't asked for reduced motion.

questions.q: What do the four WCAG principles (POUR) stand for?
questions.explain: WCAG 2.2 is current and each version is backwards compatible.

questions.q: Roughly what share of people worldwide live with a significant disability, per the WHO figure cited?
questions.explain: Nearly everyone also has temporary or situational limits.

questions.q: For HTML and CSS authors, accessibility is mostly:
options: A consequence of choices like semantic elements, labels, contrast, focus styles and reflow
An extra layer added at the end
questions.explain: Levels 1 and 2 choices already carry most of it.

questions.q: Which problem especially affects people with colour vision deficiency?
questions.explain: They need no special tools; they just see colours differently.

questions.q: When does a <header> become a banner landmark?
options: When it is not inside article, aside, main, nav or section
questions.explain: In the lesson's tree, the article's header and footer did not become landmarks.

questions.q: When does a <section> become a region landmark?
options: When it has an accessible name (aria-label or aria-labelledby)
questions.explain: The unnamed section produced no region; the named one did.

questions.q: Which landmarks are always exposed regardless of context?
questions.explain: A form is a landmark only when named.

questions.q: How do most screen-reader users primarily navigate a page?
options: By headings, with landmarks to skip whole regions
questions.explain: Both are cheap to get right and have a huge payoff.

questions.q: Which elements are skipped by Tab in the lesson's test?
options: div with onclick, a without href, disabled button and tabindex=-1 element
questions.explain: Adding onclick doesn't make anything focusable.

questions.q: Why did the input with tabindex="3" receive focus first?
options: It was first in the source
Positive tabindex values jump ahead of the natural order
questions.explain: It was fifth in the source; positive values are best avoided.

questions.q: Which keys activate links and buttons?
options: Links with Enter only; buttons with Enter and Space
questions.explain: A reason not to fake one with the other.

questions.q: What is the WCAG 2.1.1 rule?
options: Everything a mouse user can do, a keyboard user must be able to do
All pages need a skip link
questions.explain: It's also the easiest requirement to test yourself.

questions.q: What does ARIA change?
options: Only what's announced in the accessibility tree, never how anything behaves
questions.explain: So a widget role obliges you to implement the keyboard behaviour.

questions.q: In the lesson's test, what happened with <div role="button">?
options: It was not reached by Tab and had 0 activations from Enter and Space, while a real button had 2
questions.explain: Tab order was ["real", "body"].

questions.q: What is the first rule of ARIA use?
options: If a native HTML element does the job, use it
questions.explain: A button beats div role=button every time.

questions.q: Which of the five rules concerns focusable elements?
options: Don't use role=presentation or aria-hidden=true on a focusable element
questions.explain: Rule 4; rule 5 requires an accessible name on every interactive element.

questions.q: What did axe-core miss in the bad form but is the worst problem?
options: The div with a click handler as 'Send', which no keyboard user can use to submit
questions.explain: Automated checks are a floor, not a ceiling.

questions.q: How should a hint be connected to its input?
options: Outside the label, linked with aria-describedby
questions.explain: It's then read after the name.

questions.q: Why is placeholder a poor label?
options: It vanishes on input and has low contrast by default
questions.explain: It passed axe only as a fallback accessible name.

questions.q: How should required fields be marked?
options: In text, not just a red asterisk; if most are required say so and mark the optional ones
questions.explain: The required attribute also exposes the state to assistive technology.

questions.q: What does an @container rule query?
options: The nearest ancestor that is a query container, never the element itself
questions.explain: An element's styles can't depend on its own size, or it could loop forever.

questions.q: In the lesson's test, a card inside a 300px container versus an 800px container produced:
options: One column at 300px; "160px 624px" (image plus text) at 800px
questions.explain: The same component and CSS gave two layouts, decided by the slot.

questions.q: What happens when the card has no container ancestor?
options: The @container rule never matches and the base styles apply as the fallback
questions.explain: The third card measured one 800px column.

questions.q: Which container-type should you almost always use?
questions.explain: container-type: size on a plain div with a paragraph measured 0px tall, because size containment ignores the children's height.

questions.q: How do :is() and :where() differ?
options: Specificity: :is() takes its most specific argument's; :where() is always zero
questions.explain: :where() suits resets and library defaults that any single class can override.

questions.q: What does "forgiving" selector list mean?
options: Invalid arguments in :is()/:where() are dropped and the rest still work, whereas a plain list is discarded entirely
questions.explain: The lesson's test: p, p:unknown-thing was discarded (black), but :is(h1, h1:unknown-thing) still made h1 blue.

questions.q: What does .card:has(img) select?
questions.explain: It's more general than a 'parent selector': h2:has(+ p) matches by a following sibling.

questions.q: Which three needs used to require a preprocessor or JavaScript but are now native?
options: Selecting by contents (:has), nesting, and controlling which stylesheet wins (@layer)
questions.explain: Covered as :has(), CSS nesting and cascade layers.

questions.q: Why list transition properties explicitly instead of transition: all?
options: all animates unintended changes (theme switches, resizes) and makes debugging harder
questions.explain: Shorthand order is property duration timing-function delay.

questions.q: Which timing function suits things entering the screen, and which things leaving?
options: ease-out for entering, ease-in for leaving
ease-in for entering, ease-out for leaving
questions.explain: linear suits spinners and progress; ease-in-out suits movement between positions.

questions.q: What are typical durations for UI feedback?
options: 100–200ms for hovers and presses, 200–400ms for moves across the screen
questions.explain: Longer feels sluggish.

questions.q: Why respect the reduced-motion media query?
options: Motion can cause dizziness and nausea for people with vestibular disorders
questions.explain: The media query lets people who want less motion get it.

questions.q: What happens when several <details> elements share the same name attribute?
options: Opening one closes the others, making an exclusive accordion
questions.explain: The lesson's test gave [false, true] after opening the first, then the second. Use it sparingly, because people often want to compare answers.

questions.q: What happens to closed <details> content in the accessibility tree?
options: It is absent, not just visually hidden
questions.explain: In Chromium it is still findable with find-in-page, which opens the details automatically.

questions.q: Which interactions toggle a <summary>?
questions.explain: It's focusable, and a toggle event fires if you need script.

questions.q: Why did JavaScript libraries for disclosures and modals often have bugs?
options: Focus management, Escape handling, stacking and ARIA state are hard to get right
questions.explain: Native elements are keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly with little or no script.

questions.q: How should the tabs component behave for the keyboard?
options: One Tab stop for the tab list, arrow keys and Home/End move between tabs, panels labelled by their tabs
Every tab is a Tab stop
questions.explain: It follows the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices pattern.

questions.q: How does the 'Save recipe' toggle expose its state?
options: aria-pressed, with a status message announced through a live region
questions.explain: Requirement 2.

questions.q: How is the confirmation dialog built and opened?
options: With <dialog> and showModal(), reporting what the user chose
questions.explain: Requirement 4.

questions.q: How was the reference solution tested?
options: Validated, audited with axe-core in both colour schemes at three widths, and driven entirely from the keyboard by a Playwright script
questions.explain: The dialog and popover were open during the audit.

questions.q: About how much time does the browser have per frame at 60 fps?
questions.explain: This budget covers JavaScript, style, layout, paint and composite.

questions.q: Which stages run when you change transform or opacity on an element with its own layer?
questions.explain: That's why animating transform and opacity is recommended. Changing width runs layout, paint and composite.

questions.q: What is layout thrashing?
options: Alternating style writes and geometry reads, like offsetWidth, which forces a synchronous layout each iteration
questions.explain: Normally layout happens once per frame, lazily.

questions.q: Which stage runs for changes to color, background or box-shadow, but not layout?
questions.explain: Geometry changes (width, margin, font-size) additionally run layout.

questions.q: What are the 'good' thresholds for LCP and CLS?
questions.explain: Measured at the 75th percentile of real visits; INP is mostly about JavaScript and rendering work.

questions.q: In the lesson's test with a 1.5 s delayed stylesheet, what was first-contentful-paint with a blocking <link>?
questions.explain: The text stayed invisible while the CSS was in flight; the media="print" + onload trick painted in about 16–24 ms.

questions.q: Why is the media="print" onload trick not a fix by itself?
options: Repainting with different styles 1.5 s later is a worse experience than waiting
questions.explain: The real technique combines it with inlined critical CSS.

questions.q: Why is CSS render-blocking?
options: Otherwise the browser would paint unstyled content and then restyle it
questions.explain: It avoids a flash of unstyled content.

questions.q: In BEM, what do the parts of recipe-card--featured and recipe-card__title mean?
options: Block recipe-card; --featured is a modifier (variant), __title is an element (part)
questions.explain: Selectors are single classes, so specificity stays flat at (0,1,0).

questions.q: Which are the four problems every CSS methodology addresses?
options: Global scope, specificity escalation, dead code, coupling to markup structure
questions.explain: For example, .sidebar ul li a breaks when someone adds a div.

questions.q: Why does BEM allow safe deletion?
options: When no HTML uses recipe-card, all its CSS can go
questions.explain: The cost is verbose class names.

questions.q: What does utility-first CSS do?
options: Provides small single-purpose classes composed in the HTML, so the stylesheet stops growing
questions.explain: Examples: flex, gap-4, p-4, rounded-lg.

questions.q: What are the three tiers of tokens?
questions.explain: Each tier refers only to the tier below.

questions.q: Why should components use semantic tokens rather than primitives like --orange-700?
options: Otherwise a dark theme can't fix it without editing the component
questions.explain: Themes remap semantic tokens.

questions.q: What do component tokens such as --button-bg provide?
options: Customisation points without leaking internals; variants become one-line overrides
questions.explain: For example, .button--danger { --button-bg: var(--color-danger); }.

questions.q: Why are custom properties the natural way to implement tokens?
options: They cascade, inherit, can be redefined per theme or subtree, and are readable from JavaScript
questions.explain: A token is a named design decision.

questions.q: Why set direction with the dir attribute rather than the CSS direction property?
options: Direction is content meaning (column order, bidi text, assistive tech), and markup is where meaning lives
questions.explain: dir accepts ltr, rtl or auto.

questions.q: What does margin-inline-start refer to?
options: The start of the inline axis: left in English, right in Arabic
questions.explain: One stylesheet then works for every direction and writing mode.

questions.q: Which pair maps physical to logical correctly?
options: width → inline-size, text-align: left → text-align: start
questions.explain: height maps to block-size in horizontal writing modes.

questions.q: What does dir="auto" do?
options: Decides direction from the first strong character in the content, useful for user-generated text
questions.explain: lang separately sets pronunciation, hyphenation and font selection.

questions.q: What is the purpose of rel="canonical"?
options: Tell search engines which of several URLs for the same content is the real one
questions.explain: Use an absolute URL; the canonical must return 200 and not be blocked.

questions.q: Is the meta description a ranking lever?
options: No: it's your pitch in the results, and search engines may write their own snippet
questions.explain: The lesson stresses that ranking weights are proprietary and anyone claiming exact weights is guessing.

questions.q: What HTML-level things genuinely help search and people alike?
options: Descriptive title and single matching h1, headings, real text and alt, descriptive link text, fast stable pages, semantic HTML
questions.explain: The foundation is the content.

questions.q: What is good practice for titles?
options: Unique per page, specific, most important words first, since results truncate by pixel width
questions.explain: Front-load the important words.

questions.q: Why is <link rel="stylesheet" href="print.css" media="print"> not render-blocking for the screen?
options: A print stylesheet isn't needed to render the screen
questions.explain: Print rules otherwise live in @media print.

questions.q: How does a print stylesheet make links useful on paper?
questions.explain: Fragment and javascript: links get empty content.

questions.q: What do break-after: avoid on headings and break-inside: avoid on figures and tables do?
options: Keep headings with what follows and keep those blocks from splitting across pages
questions.explain: orphans and widows of 3 keep at least 3 lines at page top or bottom.

questions.q: How big is 12pt in CSS pixels?
options: 16px, the same as the screen default
questions.explain: pt, cm, mm and in are the natural units for paper.

questions.q: What does a browser do with a declaration it doesn't understand?
options: Skips just that declaration; unknown selectors skip the rule, unknown at-rules skip the block
questions.explain: That makes fallbacks trivial: declare the safe value first, the new one second.

questions.q: For .b { background: rgb(200,0,0); background: color-mix(in oklch, red, blue); } what does an old browser without color-mix() render?
questions.explain: Each browser keeps the last declaration it understands.

questions.q: Which case does the fallback-first pattern not protect?
options: Declarations using var(), since they can't be checked at parse time
questions.explain: A comma-separated selector list is also all-or-nothing unless you use :is() or :where().

questions.q: What is progressive enhancement?
options: Build a baseline that works everywhere, then layer improvements for browsers that support them
questions.explain: It lets you use new features without breaking the page for others.

questions.q: Why must HTML and CSS be checked automatically on every change?
options: They fail silently: browsers repair invalid markup and ignore invalid declarations without errors
Browsers refuse to render invalid code
questions.explain: A typo, missing label or skipped heading level produces no error.

questions.q: Which tool catches missing names, contrast and ARIA misuse automatically?
questions.explain: Stylelint checks CSS correctness; html-validate checks markup.

questions.q: What can only manual review judge?
options: Meaningful alt text and sensible reading order, using a screen reader and keyboard
questions.explain: Automation is a floor, not a ceiling.

questions.q: For pages built by JavaScript, what should you validate?
options: The rendered DOM, e.g. page.content() in Playwright
questions.explain: Validators check the source file by default.

questions.q: What are the cascade layers in the capstone, in order?
options: reset, tokens, base, layout, components, utilities, print
questions.explain: Later layers win over earlier ones.

questions.q: How is the speakers section built?
options: An auto-fit grid of container-query cards
A flex row with fixed widths
questions.explain: Requirement 6.

questions.q: How must the registration form handle errors?
options: Inline errors plus an error summary, and a status message on success
questions.explain: Requirement 7.

questions.q: What does the quality pipeline include?
options: html-validate, Stylelint with a specificity budget, axe-core in light and dark at 360/800/1280px, and Playwright in two engines
questions.explain: The fictional event page says so openly.

questions.q: With box-sizing: content-box, `.box { width: 200px; padding: 20px; border: 5px solid; }` renders how wide in total?
questions.explain: Content 200 + padding 2×20 + border 2×5 = 250px. With border-box it would be 200px.

questions.q: Two rules match one span: `#a .b { color: red }` and `.b.c.d { color: blue }`. The span has classes b c d inside #a. Which colour wins?
options: Blue: three classes beat one ID
Red: one ID outranks any number of classes
questions.explain: Specificity compares IDs first: (1,1,0) beats (0,3,0). Verified in the browser: the computed colour was the #a rule's.

questions.q: A 600px flex container holds three items with `flex: 1`, `flex: 2` and `flex: 3`. Their widths are:
questions.explain: flex: n means n 1 0%, so all 600px is free and is split 1:2:3.

questions.q: In a 300px flex container, item A is `width: 200px` (default flex-shrink: 1) and item B is `width: 200px; flex-shrink: 0`. Final widths?
questions.explain: B refuses to shrink, so A absorbs all the 100px overflow. Measured: [100, 200].

questions.q: Two `flex: 1` items in a 300px container with `gap: 20px` are each:
questions.explain: 300 − 20 = 280 shared equally = 140px each.

questions.q: A 1000px grid uses `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr))` and has only two items. How wide is each?
questions.explain: auto-fit collapses the three empty tracks, so the two items stretch: 500px 500px. With auto-fill they would stay 200px.

questions.q: A grid has `grid-template-columns: 200px 1fr 2fr; gap: 20px` in 1000px. How wide is the 2fr column?
`.badge { position: absolute; top: 0; right: 0 }` sits inside a card that has no positioned ancestor. Where does it land?
options: The top-right corner of the page (initial containing block)
questions.explain: Add position: relative to the card to anchor it to the card.

questions.q:
For `

`, the p's padding-top is:
questions.explain: em in font-size refers to the parent (20 → 30px), but em in padding refers to the element's own font-size: 2 × 30 = 60px. Measured.

questions.q: Why does `z-index: 9999` sometimes not lift an element above another?
options: Its stacking context is trapped below the other one
questions.explain: z-index only competes within the same stacking context.

questions.q: With :root{--space:1rem} and .card{--space:2rem}, what padding does .x{padding:var(--space)} get when .x is inside .card?
options: 2rem, because custom properties inherit and are overridden per subtree
questions.explain: Custom properties are inherited, so the nearest definition wins.

questions.q: A button is `<div role="button">`. What's missing compared with `<button>`?
options: Tab focus and Enter/Space activation; ARIA only changes what's announced
questions.explain: Measured in the lesson: 0 activations and not in the tab order.

questions.q: Which `<section>` becomes a region landmark?
options: One with an accessible name (aria-labelledby or aria-label)
questions.explain: An unnamed section adds no landmark.

questions.q: A recipe form field needs a visible hint read after the label. What is the correct way?
options: A <label for> plus a hint linked with aria-describedby
Put the hint inside the label
questions.explain: Placeholders vanish and have low contrast; describedby is read after the name.

questions.q: A card should switch to a two-column layout when its own slot is wide, regardless of the viewport. Which is right?
options: container-type: inline-size on the wrapper plus @container (width >= 30rem)
questions.explain: @container queries the nearest container ancestor, never the element itself.

questions.q: Which change is cheapest to animate (style then composite only)?
questions.explain: Layout properties force layout and paint every frame.

questions.q: Why prefer `padding-inline-start` over `padding-left` in a site that has Arabic pages?
options: It follows the text direction, so one stylesheet works in LTR and RTL
questions.explain: Logical properties flip automatically with dir="rtl".

questions.q: Which pair of tokens follows the three-tier approach correctly?
questions.explain: Themes remap semantic tokens, so components should reference those.

questions.q: `.a { display:block; display:not-a-real-value }` in a browser that doesn't understand the second value. What happens?
options: The unknown declaration is dropped and block stays
questions.explain: Unknown CSS is skipped declaration by declaration, which makes fallbacks trivial.

challenges.title: Proportional flex columns
challenges.prompt: A .row is a 600px flex container with three <i> items. Write CSS so the items are 100px, 200px and 300px wide, using flex-grow only (no widths). Assume `.row { display:flex; width:600px }` and items `.a`, `.b`, `.c`.
challenges.explain: With a basis of 0 all 600px is free space, shared 1:2:3. Verified by measuring the rendered widths: [100, 200, 300].

challenges.title: Auto-fitting gallery
challenges.prompt: Make `.gallery` a grid that fits as many columns of at least 200px as will fit and stretches them. In a 1000px container with two items, the items must each be 500px wide.
challenges.explain: auto-fit collapses the three empty tracks to 0px, so the two items stretch to 500px. Verified: getComputedStyle gave "500px 500px 0px 0px 0px".
